scope: Follow-up read-only review of the compact NumPy recompute implementation after producer, prefix, and input pin fixes. Synthetic packet tests only; no real P6 output or model run inspected.

resolved_findings.resolution: Prefix receipts now require baseline primary role, prefix_reexecution=true, prefix mode/chain/zero eta and expected horizon; endpoint and result metadata must report exact matched parity for n+1 checkpoints; incoming files must bind the complete V5 baseline ledger and immediately preceding FP32 cotangent.

Offline result now reports per-window max-absolute, RMS, and relative-L2 difference between local pre-cast FP64 and promoted returned FP32. These are clearly local narrowing diagnostics, not a global FP64 gradient.

Each receipt role is hard-pinned to the frozen V5 baseline or P6 source/executable IDs and corresponding protocol SHA; all receipts must use the registered input hash, and all six primary cases must share the preserved baseline namelist hash.

negative_fixtures.mutation: baseline_prefix_224 claimed plus_0p01/non-prefix role and false endpoint parity
P6 prefix receipt assigned V5 producer IDs
P6 prefix receipt assigned V5 protocol SHA
plus_0p01 registered WRF input hash changed
negative_fixtures.result: rejected as registered input hash mismatch

negative_fixtures.mutation: plus_0p01 primary namelist hash differs from preserved baseline

formula_and_scope: FD equations, shared denominator, signal floor, one-sided slopes, signed-zero byte checks, FP32 chain cast equality, and no-global-FP64-gradient/replay disclaimers remain as reviewed. No actual P6 gradient or FD result is claimed.
remaining_boundary: This unblocks recompute source/metadata review only. Final real-packet review must still check the completed receipts, NPZ/manifest hashes, and actual Fortran FP32 chain after g0 exists.
